islam_2_108.meaning: It cautions against demanding the Prophet to answer questions as Moses was asked, and warns that swapping faith for disbelief leads one away from the straight path.
islam_2_108.text: It cautions against demanding the Prophet to answer questions as Moses was asked, and warns that swapping faith for disbelief leads one away from the straight path.

islam_2_107.meaning: The passage affirms Allah’s ownership of the heavens and earth, reminding humanity that no protector or helper exists besides Him, reinforcing monotheistic reliance in all affairs of life.
islam_2_107.text: The passage affirms Allah’s ownership of the heavens and earth, reminding humanity that no protector or helper exists besides Him, reinforcing monotheistic reliance in all affairs of life.

islam_2_112.meaning: Those who sincerely submit to Allah in Islam and perform good deeds receive reward from their Lord, facing no fear or grief in the hereafter.
islam_2_112.text: Those who sincerely submit to Allah in Islam and perform good deeds receive reward from their Lord, facing no fear or grief in the hereafter.

islam_2_111.meaning: Claim that only Jews or Christians can enter Paradise is rejected; believers are asked to present evidence if their assertion is truthful, before accountability, emphasizing responsibility.
islam_2_111.text: Claim that only Jews or Christians can enter Paradise is rejected; believers are asked to present evidence if their assertion is truthful, before accountability, emphasizing responsibility.

islam_2_110.meaning: Establishing prayer and giving zakah are linked to personal benefit; every good deed is recorded by Allah, who observes all actions and rewards accordingly in this world and the next.
islam_2_110.text: Establishing prayer and giving zakah are linked to personal benefit; every good deed is recorded by Allah, who observes all actions and rewards accordingly in this world and the next.

islam_2_114.meaning: The verse condemns those who forbid the name of God from being invoked in mosques and seek their ruin; such people may only enter out of fear, and they face worldly disgrace and punishment in the hereafter.
islam_2_114.text: The verse condemns those who forbid the name of God from being invoked in mosques and seek their ruin; such people may only enter out of fear, and they face worldly disgrace and punishment in the hereafter.

islam_2_115.meaning: It declares that direction belongs to God; the east and west are under His dominion, so wherever a person faces, they encounter God’s presence. The verse emphasizes Allah’s all encompassing knowledge and sovereignty.
islam_2_115.text: It declares that direction belongs to God; the east and west are under His dominion, so wherever a person faces, they encounter God’s presence. The verse emphasizes Allah’s all encompassing knowledge and sovereignty.

islam_2_117.meaning: God is described as the Originator of the heavens and earth; His command 'Be' instantly creates reality, illustrating divine authority and the effortless nature of creation in Islamic theology.
islam_2_117.text: God is described as the Originator of the heavens and earth; His command 'Be' instantly creates reality, illustrating divine authority and the effortless nature of creation in Islamic theology.

islam_2_116.meaning: The passage refutes the claim that God has a son, affirming His exalted status; everything in heaven and earth belongs to Him, and all creation submits obediently to His will.
islam_2_116.text: The passage refutes the claim that God has a son, affirming His exalted status; everything in heaven and earth belongs to Him, and all creation submits obediently to His will.

islam_2_118.meaning: Those ignorant question why God does not speak or send signs, echoing earlier peoples’ doubts; the verse notes their similar hardened hearts and affirms that clear signs have been given to the convinced.
islam_2_118.text: Those ignorant question why God does not speak or send signs, echoing earlier peoples’ doubts; the verse notes their similar hardened hearts and affirms that clear signs have been given to the convinced.

islam_2_113.meaning: Jews and Christians each claim the other lacks foundation despite citing scripture; polytheists echo similar disputes, while ultimate judgment rests with Allah over all humanity.
islam_2_113.text: Jews and Christians each claim the other lacks foundation despite citing scripture; polytheists echo similar disputes, while ultimate judgment rests with Allah over all humanity.

islam_2_121.meaning: People who possess the Scripture recite it accurately, believing its message; those who reject it are described as the true losers, underscoring belief versus denial as a decisive moral divide.
islam_2_121.text: People who possess the Scripture recite it accurately, believing its message; those who reject it are described as the true losers, underscoring belief versus denial as a decisive moral divide.

islam_2_119.meaning: God announces sending the Prophet with truth, as a bearer of glad tidings and warning; the messenger will not be held accountable for the fate of those destined for Hell.
islam_2_119.text: God announces sending the Prophet with truth, as a bearer of glad tidings and warning; the messenger will not be held accountable for the fate of those destined for Hell.

islam_2_123.meaning: The warning urges fear of the Day when no soul can aid another, no compensation is accepted, and intercession fails; everyone will be left to face divine judgment alone.
islam_2_123.text: The warning urges fear of the Day when no soul can aid another, no compensation is accepted, and intercession fails; everyone will be left to face divine judgment alone.

islam_2_124.meaning: Abraham obeyed God's commands, proving his faith; God promised him leadership over humanity, but Abraham asked if his descendants would share it. God replied that the covenant excludes those who act unjustly.
islam_2_124.text: Abraham obeyed God's commands, proving his faith; God promised him leadership over humanity, but Abraham asked if his descendants would share it. God replied that the covenant excludes those who act unjustly.

islam_2_120.meaning: The verse predicts that Jews and Christians will not accept the Prophet unless he adopts their religion; it commands following divine guidance alone, warning that yielding to their desires would lead to loss.
islam_2_120.text: The verse predicts that Jews and Christians will not accept the Prophet unless he adopts their religion; it commands following divine guidance alone, warning that yielding to their desires would lead to loss.

islam_2_122.meaning: Addressed to the Israelites, God recalls His blessings upon them and states that He chose them above all nations, highlighting a special covenant and their elevated status in earlier revelation.
islam_2_122.text: Addressed to the Israelites, God recalls His blessings upon them and states that He chose them above all nations, highlighting a special covenant and their elevated status in earlier revelation.

islam_2_126.meaning: Abraham prayed for Mecca to become a protected city, its inhabitants blessed with abundant fruit, and that believers would prosper while disbelievers receive brief worldly pleasure before divine judgment.
islam_2_126.text: Abraham prayed for Mecca to become a protected city, its inhabitants blessed with abundant fruit, and that believers would prosper while disbelievers receive brief worldly pleasure before divine judgment.

islam_2_127.meaning: While constructing the Kaaba, Abraham and his son Ishmael raised its foundations, invoking God to accept their work, acknowledging Him as all-hearing and all-knowing in this sacred endeavor.
islam_2_127.text: While constructing the Kaaba, Abraham and his son Ishmael raised its foundations, invoking God to accept their work, acknowledging Him as all-hearing and all-knowing in this sacred endeavor.

islam_2_125.meaning: God designated the Kaaba as a focal point for pilgrimage and safety, instructed Abraham and Ishmael to establish a place of worship there, and commanded them to cleanse the sanctuary for pilgrims performing tawaf.
islam_2_125.text: God designated the Kaaba as a focal point for pilgrimage and safety, instructed Abraham and Ishmael to establish a place of worship there, and commanded them to cleanse the sanctuary for pilgrims performing tawaf.

islam_2_130.meaning: Rejecting Abraham’s faith is self-destructive; God chose Abraham in this world and guarantees his ultimate status among the righteous in the afterlife, highlighting his exemplary devotion.
islam_2_130.text: Rejecting Abraham’s faith is self-destructive; God chose Abraham in this world and guarantees his ultimate status among the righteous in the afterlife, highlighting his exemplary devotion.

islam_2_129.meaning: They prayed for a messenger from among their people to recite divine verses, teach scripture and wisdom, and purify the community, affirming God’s supreme power and wisdom.
islam_2_129.text: They prayed for a messenger from among their people to recite divine verses, teach scripture and wisdom, and purify the community, affirming God’s supreme power and wisdom.

islam_2_128.meaning: They asked God to make them devoted worshippers, to guide their descendants as a faithful community, to reveal proper rites, and to accept their repentance, emphasizing His mercy and willingness to forgive.
islam_2_128.text: They asked God to make them devoted worshippers, to guide their descendants as a faithful community, to reveal proper rites, and to accept their repentance, emphasizing His mercy and willingness to forgive.

islam_2_133.meaning: Jacob, nearing death, asked his children which deity they would worship; they affirmed worship of his God, the same God of Abraham, Ishmael, and Isaac, declaring unity and their Muslim identity.
islam_2_133.text: Jacob, nearing death, asked his children which deity they would worship; they affirmed worship of his God, the same God of Abraham, Ishmael, and Isaac, declaring unity and their Muslim identity.

islam_2_134.meaning: It reminds believers that previous peoples receive recompense for their deeds, and each community is accountable only for its own actions, a theme in Qur'an emphasizing personal responsibility.
islam_2_134.text: It reminds believers that previous peoples receive recompense for their deeds, and each community is accountable only for its own actions, a theme in Qur'an emphasizing personal responsibility.

islam_2_135.meaning: The verse rejects the claim that Jews or Christians alone hold truth, asserting that Abraham's monotheistic faith (Hanif) is the original, pure submission to Allah, distinct from polytheism.
islam_2_135.text: The verse rejects the claim that Jews or Christians alone hold truth, asserting that Abraham's monotheistic faith (Hanif) is the original, pure submission to Allah, distinct from polytheism.

islam_2_136.meaning: It calls believers to affirm faith in Allah, the revelations given to Muhammad, and the earlier scriptures given to Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, Moses, Jesus, and all prophets, emphasizing continuity.
islam_2_136.text: It calls believers to affirm faith in Allah, the revelations given to Muhammad, and the earlier scriptures given to Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, Moses, Jesus, and all prophets, emphasizing continuity.

islam_2_131.meaning: When God commanded Abraham to submit, he responded by declaring his total surrender to the Lord of all worlds, exemplifying complete obedience and his unwavering trust in divine guidance.
islam_2_131.text: When God commanded Abraham to submit, he responded by declaring his total surrender to the Lord of all worlds, exemplifying complete obedience and his unwavering trust in divine guidance.

islam_2_132.meaning: Abraham urged his sons and grandson Jacob to remain steadfast in the monotheistic religion God chose for them, urging them not to die except as true believers.
islam_2_132.text: Abraham urged his sons and grandson Jacob to remain steadfast in the monotheistic religion God chose for them, urging them not to die except as true believers.

islam_2_139.meaning: Challenges opponents who argue about Allah, affirming that Allah is Lord of both parties; each will be judged by their own deeds, and believers remain sincere in worship.
islam_2_139.text: Challenges opponents who argue about Allah, affirming that Allah is Lord of both parties; each will be judged by their own deeds, and believers remain sincere in worship.

islam_2_138.meaning: Declares that Islam is the religion ordained by Allah; no one surpasses Him in guiding worship, and believers submit wholly to Him as the ultimate object of devotion.
islam_2_138.text: Declares that Islam is the religion ordained by Allah; no one surpasses Him in guiding worship, and believers submit wholly to Him as the ultimate object of devotion.

islam_2_137.meaning: If others accept the same faith they are guided; if they reject it, they remain in dissent, and Allah alone suffices as protector and witness, knowing all deeds.
islam_2_137.text: If others accept the same faith they are guided; if they reject it, they remain in dissent, and Allah alone suffices as protector and witness, knowing all deeds.

islam_2_142.meaning: Addresses criticism of changing the qibla, stating that direction belongs to Allah, who controls east and west; He guides those He wills to the straight path.
islam_2_142.text: Addresses criticism of changing the qibla, stating that direction belongs to Allah, who controls east and west; He guides those He wills to the straight path.

islam_2_140.meaning: Refutes the notion that Abraham and his descendants were Jews or Christians; asks who knows better than Allah, and condemns those who hide divine testimony, stressing Allah's justice.
islam_2_140.text: Refutes the notion that Abraham and his descendants were Jews or Christians; asks who knows better than Allah, and condemns those who hide divine testimony, stressing Allah's justice.

islam_2_141.meaning: Reiterates that a past nation will bear its own outcome, and each community is responsible for its deeds, echoing the Qur'anic principle of individual accountability.
islam_2_141.text: Reiterates that a past nation will bear its own outcome, and each community is responsible for its deeds, echoing the Qur'anic principle of individual accountability.

islam_2_143.meaning: Declares the Muslim community as a just nation meant to witness humanity, with the Prophet as a witness over them; the qibla change served to test sincere followers.
islam_2_143.text: Declares the Muslim community as a just nation meant to witness humanity, with the Prophet as a witness over them; the qibla change served to test sincere followers.

islam_2_146.meaning: Refers to People of the Book who recognize Muhammad as a prophet as intimately as they know their children, yet a faction deliberately hides the truth despite clear knowledge, reflecting internal dissent.
islam_2_146.text: Refers to People of the Book who recognize Muhammad as a prophet as intimately as they know their children, yet a faction deliberately hides the truth despite clear knowledge, reflecting internal dissent.

islam_2_147.meaning: Declares that truth originates from Allah; believers are urged not to join skeptics, emphasizing reliance on divine revelation over doubt, reinforcing confidence in the Qur'anic message.
islam_2_147.text: Declares that truth originates from Allah; believers are urged not to join skeptics, emphasizing reliance on divine revelation over doubt, reinforcing confidence in the Qur'anic message.

islam_2_148.meaning: States that every nation has its own direction of worship; Muslims are encouraged to strive for righteousness, trusting that Allah will gather all humanity together on the Day of Judgment, capable of all deeds.
islam_2_148.text: States that every nation has its own direction of worship; Muslims are encouraged to strive for righteousness, trusting that Allah will gather all humanity together on the Day of Judgment, capable of all deeds.

islam_2_145.meaning: The verse addresses Jews and Christians, stating that even if all scriptural signs were shown, they would not adopt the Muslim qibla, nor would Muslims follow theirs; each community retains its own ritual orientation.
islam_2_145.text: The verse addresses Jews and Christians, stating that even if all scriptural signs were shown, they would not adopt the Muslim qibla, nor would Muslims follow theirs; each community retains its own ritual orientation.

islam_2_144.meaning: God observed the Prophet’s gaze toward the heavens, promised a new qibla pleasing to him, directing Muslims to face the Kaaba in Mecca wherever they are, establishing communal direction.
islam_2_144.text: God observed the Prophet’s gaze toward the heavens, promised a new qibla pleasing to him, directing Muslims to face the Kaaba in Mecca wherever they are, establishing communal direction.

islam_2_150.meaning: Reiterates facing the Sacred Mosque from any location, aiming to prevent disputes among people; only those who commit wrongdoing may object, urging fear of Allah and unity.
islam_2_150.text: Reiterates facing the Sacred Mosque from any location, aiming to prevent disputes among people; only those who commit wrongdoing may object, urging fear of Allah and unity.

islam_2_149.meaning: Commands believers to orient prayer toward the Sacred Mosque wherever they travel, affirming this direction as divine truth, and reminds that Allah fully observes all actions, reinforcing accountability.
islam_2_149.text: Commands believers to orient prayer toward the Sacred Mosque wherever they travel, affirming this direction as divine truth, and reminds that Allah fully observes all actions, reinforcing accountability.

islam_2_151.meaning: Highlights that God sent Muhammad, a messenger from among humanity, to recite divine verses, purify believers, convey scripture, wisdom, and previously unknown knowledge, establishing guidance and moral reform.
islam_2_151.text: Highlights that God sent Muhammad, a messenger from among humanity, to recite divine verses, purify believers, convey scripture, wisdom, and previously unknown knowledge, establishing guidance and moral reform.

islam_2_153.meaning: Addresses the faithful, urging reliance on patience and the five daily prayers as sources of divine assistance; assures that steadfast believers receive Allah’s support, emphasizing perseverance.
islam_2_153.text: Addresses the faithful, urging reliance on patience and the five daily prayers as sources of divine assistance; assures that steadfast believers receive Allah’s support, emphasizing perseverance.

islam_2_154.meaning: The Qur'an states that those slain in jihad are not dead but alive in God's knowledge, unseen by humans; this affirms belief in the after-life and honors martyrs' spiritual status.
islam_2_154.text: The Qur'an states that those slain in jihad are not dead but alive in God's knowledge, unseen by humans; this affirms belief in the after-life and honors martyrs' spiritual status.

islam_2_152.meaning: Calls believers to remember Allah, promising divine remembrance in return; encourages gratitude and warns against denial, linking remembrance with spiritual benefit and moral responsibility for humanity.
islam_2_152.text: Calls believers to remember Allah, promising divine remembrance in return; encourages gratitude and warns against denial, linking remembrance with spiritual benefit and moral responsibility for humanity.

islam_2_157.meaning: Those who utter this creed receive God's blessings and mercy, and are described as guided, indicating that sincere acknowledgment of divine sovereignty leads to spiritual success and divine favor.
islam_2_157.text: Those who utter this creed receive God's blessings and mercy, and are described as guided, indicating that sincere acknowledgment of divine sovereignty leads to spiritual success and divine favor.

islam_2_158.meaning: Safa and Marwah, the two hills near Mecca, are sacred symbols; pilgrims performing Hajj or Umrah may walk between them without sin, and voluntary good deeds are praised by Allah.
islam_2_158.text: Safa and Marwah, the two hills near Mecca, are sacred symbols; pilgrims performing Hajj or Umrah may walk between them without sin, and voluntary good deeds are praised by Allah.

islam_2_159.meaning: Those who hide clear revelations after they have been made evident are cursed by God and by those who curse, underscoring the severe condemnation of concealing divine guidance.
islam_2_159.text: Those who hide clear revelations after they have been made evident are cursed by God and by those who curse, underscoring the severe condemnation of concealing divine guidance.

islam_2_160.meaning: God promises forgiveness to those who sincerely repent, amend their ways, and openly demonstrate change; He affirms Himself as the Most Merciful and Accepting of repentance.
islam_2_160.text: God promises forgiveness to those who sincerely repent, amend their ways, and openly demonstrate change; He affirms Himself as the Most Merciful and Accepting of repentance.

islam_2_155.meaning: God warns believers they will face trials such as fear, hunger, loss of wealth, lives, and crops, yet promises reward to those who endure patiently, linking perseverance with divine glad tidings.
islam_2_155.text: God warns believers they will face trials such as fear, hunger, loss of wealth, lives, and crops, yet promises reward to those who endure patiently, linking perseverance with divine glad tidings.

islam_2_156.meaning: When calamity strikes, true believers respond with the declaration that all belongs to Allah and they will return to Him, expressing submission, trust, and awareness of ultimate accountability.
islam_2_156.text: When calamity strikes, true believers respond with the declaration that all belongs to Allah and they will return to Him, expressing submission, trust, and awareness of ultimate accountability.

islam_2_161.meaning: Disbelievers who die without renouncing disbelief incur the curse of Allah, angels, and all humanity, reflecting Qur'anic teaching that persistent rejection of faith leads to collective condemnation.
islam_2_161.text: Disbelievers who die without renouncing disbelief incur the curse of Allah, angels, and all humanity, reflecting Qur'anic teaching that persistent rejection of faith leads to collective condemnation.

islam_2_164.meaning: The verse points to natural signs of God: the heavens and earth, the regular shift between night and day, sea vessels that transport useful goods, and rain descending from the sky that revives all living things.
islam_2_164.text: The verse points to natural signs of God: the heavens and earth, the regular shift between night and day, sea vessels that transport useful goods, and rain descending from the sky that revives all living things.

islam_2_162.meaning: The cursed will remain eternally in Hell, with no reduction or reprieve of punishment, emphasizing the irrevocable nature of divine retribution for those who reject truth.
islam_2_162.text: The cursed will remain eternally in Hell, with no reduction or reprieve of punishment, emphasizing the irrevocable nature of divine retribution for those who reject truth.

islam_2_166.meaning: When leaders abandon their followers, the latter observe the ensuing divine punishment, prompting them to cut off relationships with those former leaders, illustrating the breakdown of loyalty after accountability.
islam_2_166.text: When leaders abandon their followers, the latter observe the ensuing divine punishment, prompting them to cut off relationships with those former leaders, illustrating the breakdown of loyalty after accountability.

islam_2_167.meaning: The followers will lament, wishing for a second chance to distance themselves as the disbelievers have, while God reveals their actions as sources of remorse, ensuring they never attain salvation.
islam_2_167.text: The followers will lament, wishing for a second chance to distance themselves as the disbelievers have, while God reveals their actions as sources of remorse, ensuring they never attain salvation.

islam_2_165.meaning: Certain individuals elevate others to God’s status, loving them as they love the Divine; believers reserve a deeper love for God alone, and the verse warns that true awareness of punishment would cause the transgressors to reflect.
islam_2_165.text: Certain individuals elevate others to God’s status, loving them as they love the Divine; believers reserve a deeper love for God alone, and the verse warns that true awareness of punishment would cause the transgressors to reflect.

islam_2_169.meaning: Satan incites believers toward wrongdoing, immoral behavior, and fabricating statements about God that lack knowledge, thereby leading them away from truth and righteousness in their daily lives.
islam_2_169.text: Satan incites believers toward wrongdoing, immoral behavior, and fabricating statements about God that lack knowledge, thereby leading them away from truth and righteousness in their daily lives.

islam_2_171.meaning: The disbelievers are compared to livestock (deaf, mute, and blind) that ignore calls and cries, symbolizing their spiritual insensitivity and refusal to comprehend divine guidance in matters of faith.
islam_2_171.text: The disbelievers are compared to livestock (deaf, mute, and blind) that ignore calls and cries, symbolizing their spiritual insensitivity and refusal to comprehend divine guidance in matters of faith.

islam_2_168.meaning: Humanity is urged to eat only what is lawful and wholesome, and to reject Satan’s influence, since he is presented as an unmistakable adversary to human well-being.
islam_2_168.text: Humanity is urged to eat only what is lawful and wholesome, and to reject Satan’s influence, since he is presented as an unmistakable adversary to human well-being.

islam_2_173.meaning: The verse lists prohibited foods, carrion, blood, pork, and items consecrated to other deities, yet exempts those forced to consume them without intent or excess, emphasizing God’s mercy and forgiveness.
islam_2_173.text: The verse lists prohibited foods, carrion, blood, pork, and items consecrated to other deities, yet exempts those forced to consume them without intent or excess, emphasizing God’s mercy and forgiveness.

islam_2_172.meaning: Believers are instructed to consume lawful, wholesome provisions provided by God and to express gratitude toward Him, affirming that true worship includes thankfulness for sustenance.
islam_2_172.text: Believers are instructed to consume lawful, wholesome provisions provided by God and to express gratitude toward Him, affirming that true worship includes thankfulness for sustenance.

islam_2_170.meaning: They respond to the call for adherence to divine revelation by insisting on following ancestral practices, despite acknowledging that their forebears were ignorant and unguided, highlighting stubborn attachment to tradition over truth.
islam_2_170.text: They respond to the call for adherence to divine revelation by insisting on following ancestral practices, despite acknowledging that their forebears were ignorant and unguided, highlighting stubborn attachment to tradition over truth.

islam_2_174.meaning: Those who hide divine revelation for worldly profit are warned they will only taste Hellfire, hear no speech from Allah on Resurrection, and receive no purification.
islam_2_174.text: Those who hide divine revelation for worldly profit are warned they will only taste Hellfire, hear no speech from Allah on Resurrection, and receive no purification.

islam_2_175.meaning: People who exchange true guidance for falsehood and mercy for punishment are described as willingly enduring the blaze, illustrating their deliberate choice of spiritual ruin.
islam_2_175.text: People who exchange true guidance for falsehood and mercy for punishment are described as willingly enduring the blaze, illustrating their deliberate choice of spiritual ruin.

islam_2_176.meaning: Allah revealed the Book with absolute truth; those who argue over its verses create deep discord, reflecting early conflicts among believers about interpretation and authenticity.
islam_2_176.text: Allah revealed the Book with absolute truth; those who argue over its verses create deep discord, reflecting early conflicts among believers about interpretation and authenticity.

islam_2_177.meaning: Righteousness is not merely facing east or west, it encompasses belief in Allah, the Last Day, angels, the Book, prophets, and giving wealth, despite attachment, to kin, orphans, and the needy.
islam_2_177.text: Righteousness is not merely facing east or west, it encompasses belief in Allah, the Last Day, angels, the Book, prophets, and giving wealth, despite attachment, to kin, orphans, and the needy.

islam_2_178.meaning: Equal retaliation, free for free, slave for slave, woman for woman, is prescribed for murder; if the victim’s family pardons, financial compensation (diyya) may replace retribution, emphasizing justice and mercy.
islam_2_178.text: Equal retaliation, free for free, slave for slave, woman for woman, is prescribed for murder; if the victim’s family pardons, financial compensation (diyya) may replace retribution, emphasizing justice and mercy.

islam_2_179.meaning: Qisas serves as a protective measure for society; recognizing its purpose encourages believers to act righteously, fostering social stability, deterrence of murder, and heightened moral consciousness.
islam_2_179.text: Qisas serves as a protective measure for society; recognizing its purpose encourages believers to act righteously, fostering social stability, deterrence of murder, and heightened moral consciousness.

islam_2_181.meaning: Changing a bequest after hearing it is a sin; accountability rests solely on those who modify it, underscoring Allah’s omniscience and the sanctity of witnessed wills.
islam_2_181.text: Changing a bequest after hearing it is a sin; accountability rests solely on those who modify it, underscoring Allah’s omniscience and the sanctity of witnessed wills.

islam_2_183.meaning: Fasting is mandated for believers, just as it was for earlier peoples, serving as a discipline to develop God-consciousness, self-control, and moral uprightness throughout the year.
islam_2_183.text: Fasting is mandated for believers, just as it was for earlier peoples, serving as a discipline to develop God-consciousness, self-control, and moral uprightness throughout the year.

islam_2_184.meaning: Fasting lasts a set number of days each year; those ill or traveling may postpone and make up the same count later. Able persons can feed a needy person as compensation; giving extra is commendable, though fasting remains optimal.
islam_2_184.text: Fasting lasts a set number of days each year; those ill or traveling may postpone and make up the same count later. Able persons can feed a needy person as compensation; giving extra is commendable, though fasting remains optimal.

islam_2_185.meaning: Ramadan is the month when the Qur’an was revealed as guidance and clear criteria for right and wrong. Muslims who witness its start must fast, while the sick or travelers may defer and make up later.
islam_2_185.text: Ramadan is the month when the Qur’an was revealed as guidance and clear criteria for right and wrong. Muslims who witness its start must fast, while the sick or travelers may defer and make up later.

islam_2_182.meaning: If one suspects the testator’s mistake or wrongdoing and rectifies the bequest, no blame falls upon him, reflecting Allah’s forgiving and merciful nature toward sincere correction.
islam_2_182.text: If one suspects the testator’s mistake or wrongdoing and rectifies the bequest, no blame falls upon him, reflecting Allah’s forgiving and merciful nature toward sincere correction.

islam_2_180.meaning: As death approaches, a believer must allocate bequests to parents and close kin within lawful bounds, a responsibility emphasized for the righteous to ensure fair distribution and family support.
islam_2_180.text: As death approaches, a believer must allocate bequests to parents and close kin within lawful bounds, a responsibility emphasized for the righteous to ensure fair distribution and family support.

islam_2_187.meaning: During Ramadan, sexual relations are permitted at night, described as mutual clothing that provides comfort and protection. The verse acknowledges previous human mistakes, noting divine forgiveness for sincere repentance.
islam_2_187.text: During Ramadan, sexual relations are permitted at night, described as mutual clothing that provides comfort and protection. The verse acknowledges previous human mistakes, noting divine forgiveness for sincere repentance.

islam_2_188.meaning: Muslims are prohibited from unlawfully taking others’ property or using authority to siphon public funds for personal gain, especially when they are aware such actions are sinful.
islam_2_188.text: Muslims are prohibited from unlawfully taking others’ property or using authority to siphon public funds for personal gain, especially when they are aware such actions are sinful.

islam_2_186.meaning: God assures that He is near whenever believers call upon Him, answering sincere prayers. He invites them to respond with belief and obedience, promising guidance for those who turn to Him.
islam_2_186.text: God assures that He is near whenever believers call upon Him, answering sincere prayers. He invites them to respond with belief and obedience, promising guidance for those who turn to Him.

islam_2_189.meaning: The new moon marks time for worship and pilgrimage; it is not piety to enter homes through back doors. True righteousness is fearing God and entering through the front, respecting propriety.
islam_2_189.text: The new moon marks time for worship and pilgrimage; it is not piety to enter homes through back doors. True righteousness is fearing God and entering through the front, respecting propriety.

islam_2_190.meaning: Believers may defend themselves against aggressors in God’s cause, but must avoid excess. God disapproves of any wrongdoing beyond what is justly required, emphasizing restraint and moral limits.
islam_2_190.text: Believers may defend themselves against aggressors in God’s cause, but must avoid excess. God disapproves of any wrongdoing beyond what is justly required, emphasizing restraint and moral limits.

islam_2_191.meaning: Combatants may kill opponents and expel them from lands they have seized, because oppression (fitnah) is worse than death. Fighting is forbidden inside the Sacred Mosque unless they attack first.
islam_2_191.text: Combatants may kill opponents and expel them from lands they have seized, because oppression (fitnah) is worse than death. Fighting is forbidden inside the Sacred Mosque unless they attack first.

islam_2_193.meaning: Muslims should continue struggle until oppression ends and worship returns solely to God. When hostilities cease, aggression must stop, except against those who persist in wrongdoing.
islam_2_193.text: Muslims should continue struggle until oppression ends and worship returns solely to God. When hostilities cease, aggression must stop, except against those who persist in wrongdoing.

islam_2_195.meaning: Encourages charitable spending for Allah’s cause, warns against self-destruction, and highlights that good deeds please Allah. Reflects early Muslim emphasis on communal welfare and moral responsibility.
islam_2_195.text: Encourages charitable spending for Allah’s cause, warns against self-destruction, and highlights that good deeds please Allah. Reflects early Muslim emphasis on communal welfare and moral responsibility.

islam_2_196.meaning: Orders completion of Hajj and ‘Umrah for Allah, allowing substitution of sacrificial animals if pilgrimage is impeded, and postpones shaving until the animal is slaughtered, establishing ritual sequence in pilgrimage law.
islam_2_196.text: Orders completion of Hajj and ‘Umrah for Allah, allowing substitution of sacrificial animals if pilgrimage is impeded, and postpones shaving until the animal is slaughtered, establishing ritual sequence in pilgrimage law.

islam_2_197.meaning: Defines the sacred months of Hajj, prohibiting sexual relations, disobedience, and disputes during the rites; assures Allah records all good deeds and advises pilgrims to bring sufficient provisions.
islam_2_197.text: Defines the sacred months of Hajj, prohibiting sexual relations, disobedience, and disputes during the rites; assures Allah records all good deeds and advises pilgrims to bring sufficient provisions.

islam_2_192.meaning: If enemies stop fighting, believers are commanded to accept forgiveness, as God’s nature is merciful and forgiving toward those who lay down arms and seek peace.
islam_2_192.text: If enemies stop fighting, believers are commanded to accept forgiveness, as God’s nature is merciful and forgiving toward those who lay down arms and seek peace.

islam_2_194.meaning: The verse permits retaliation (qisas) during sacred months, matching the injury inflicted, while urging believers to fear Allah, who supports the pious. It balances justice with divine protection in early Islamic law.
islam_2_194.text: The verse permits retaliation (qisas) during sacred months, matching the injury inflicted, while urging believers to fear Allah, who supports the pious. It balances justice with divine protection in early Islamic law.

islam_2_200.meaning: After completing rites, urges remembrance of Allah with the devotion once given to ancestors, warns that those who only pray for worldly gain will lack any share in the Hereafter.
islam_2_200.text: After completing rites, urges remembrance of Allah with the devotion once given to ancestors, warns that those who only pray for worldly gain will lack any share in the Hereafter.

islam_2_198.meaning: States no blame for seeking Allah’s bounty, instructs pilgrims to remember Allah after Arafat at al-Mash'ar al-Haram, and reminds them of guidance after previous misguidance.
islam_2_198.text: States no blame for seeking Allah’s bounty, instructs pilgrims to remember Allah after Arafat at al-Mash'ar al-Haram, and reminds them of guidance after previous misguidance.

islam_2_199.meaning: Directs pilgrims to depart from the gathering point, seek Allah’s forgiveness, emphasizing divine mercy and forgiveness for those who turn back together after the rites.
islam_2_199.text: Directs pilgrims to depart from the gathering point, seek Allah’s forgiveness, emphasizing divine mercy and forgiveness for those who turn back together after the rites.

islam_2_201.meaning: Highlights a balanced supplication asking for goodness in this life and the Hereafter while requesting protection from the fire, reflecting the Qur’anic model of comprehensive du’a.
islam_2_201.text: Highlights a balanced supplication asking for goodness in this life and the Hereafter while requesting protection from the fire, reflecting the Qur’anic model of comprehensive du’a.

islam_2_202.meaning: Assures that each person will receive the portion they earned, and that Allah’s reckoning is swift, reinforcing accountability and divine justice in the afterlife always.
islam_2_202.text: Assures that each person will receive the portion they earned, and that Allah’s reckoning is swift, reinforcing accountability and divine justice in the afterlife always.

islam_2_203.meaning: Reminds believers to remember Allah during the specified days of pilgrimage; whether one hastens or delays, no sin falls on the devout, who must fear Allah and anticipate the final gathering.
islam_2_203.text: Reminds believers to remember Allah during the specified days of pilgrimage; whether one hastens or delays, no sin falls on the devout, who must fear Allah and anticipate the final gathering.

islam_2_206.meaning: Depicts a stubborn individual who, when warned to fear Allah, lets pride deepen his wrongdoing; the Qur'an declares that Hellfire alone will suffice as his final abode, emphasizing divine justice.
islam_2_206.text: Depicts a stubborn individual who, when warned to fear Allah, lets pride deepen his wrongdoing; the Qur'an declares that Hellfire alone will suffice as his final abode, emphasizing divine justice.

islam_2_207.meaning: Refers to a believer who sacrifices personal gain, striving for Allah's approval; the verse assures that Allah shows kindness and generosity toward such devoted servants, rewarding sincere devotion.
islam_2_207.text: Refers to a believer who sacrifices personal gain, striving for Allah's approval; the verse assures that Allah shows kindness and generosity toward such devoted servants, rewarding sincere devotion.

islam_2_208.meaning: Calls believers to complete submission to Islam, urging total obedience and warning against imitating Satan, who is presented as a clear and relentless enemy, reinforcing the need for steadfast faith.
islam_2_208.text: Calls believers to complete submission to Islam, urging total obedience and warning against imitating Satan, who is presented as a clear and relentless enemy, reinforcing the need for steadfast faith.

islam_2_209.meaning: Warns that abandoning the faith after receiving unmistakable evidence invites Allah's supreme power and wisdom as a reminder of divine accountability, underscoring the seriousness of deliberate deviation.
islam_2_209.text: Warns that abandoning the faith after receiving unmistakable evidence invites Allah's supreme power and wisdom as a reminder of divine accountability, underscoring the seriousness of deliberate deviation.

islam_2_204.meaning: Describes a hypocrite whose smooth words win approval, yet he secretly opposes the believers, he swears by Allah to conceal his true hostility, a warning against deceptive speech common in early Medina.
islam_2_204.text: Describes a hypocrite whose smooth words win approval, yet he secretly opposes the believers, he swears by Allah to conceal his true hostility, a warning against deceptive speech common in early Medina.

islam_2_205.meaning: Refers to a person who, after leaving the community, spreads mischief across the land, destroying crops and livestock; the Qur'an condemns such 'fasad' as displeasing to Allah and harmful to society.
islam_2_205.text: Refers to a person who, after leaving the community, spreads mischief across the land, destroying crops and livestock; the Qur'an condemns such 'fasad' as displeasing to Allah and harmful to society.

islam_2_210.meaning: Poses a rhetorical question about those who expect Allah to appear in clouds with angels to settle matters, reminding that all affairs ultimately return to Allah's judgment and control.
islam_2_210.text: Poses a rhetorical question about those who expect Allah to appear in clouds with angels to settle matters, reminding that all affairs ultimately return to Allah's judgment and control.

islam_2_211.meaning: Invites reflection on the numerous signs granted to the Children of Israel, emphasizing that anyone who repays Allah's blessings with rejection will incur a severe divine penalty.
islam_2_211.text: Invites reflection on the numerous signs granted to the Children of Israel, emphasizing that anyone who repays Allah's blessings with rejection will incur a severe divine penalty.

islam_2_212.meaning: Describes how this world is presented attractively to disbelievers, who mock believers; yet those who fear Allah will be superior on Resurrection, while Allah supplies provision to whomever He chooses, without limitation.
islam_2_212.text: Describes how this world is presented attractively to disbelievers, who mock believers; yet those who fear Allah will be superior on Resurrection, while Allah supplies provision to whomever He chooses, without limitation.

islam_2_213.meaning: States that humanity originally followed a single faith, then Allah dispatched prophets bearing glad tidings and warnings, along with true scriptures to adjudicate disputes; no divergence existed before these revelations.
islam_2_213.text: States that humanity originally followed a single faith, then Allah dispatched prophets bearing glad tidings and warnings, along with true scriptures to adjudicate disputes; no divergence existed before these revelations.

islam_2_215.meaning: Guidance on charitable spending: allocate surplus to parents, relatives, orphans, the needy, and travelers; any good deed is recorded by Allah, who knows all intentions.
islam_2_215.text: Guidance on charitable spending: allocate surplus to parents, relatives, orphans, the needy, and travelers; any good deed is recorded by Allah, who knows all intentions.

islam_2_214.meaning: It reminds believers that Paradise follows trials; earlier communities endured poverty, oppression, and fear before the Prophet and his companions declared hope, showing that steadfastness amid hardship is praised.
islam_2_214.text: It reminds believers that Paradise follows trials; earlier communities endured poverty, oppression, and fear before the Prophet and his companions declared hope, showing that steadfastness amid hardship is praised.

islam_2_217.meaning: Queries about the sacred month and fighting are answered: fighting during it is serious, yet abandoning Allah’s path, denying Him, desecrating the Sacred Mosque, or expelling its people are far graver sins.
islam_2_217.text: Queries about the sacred month and fighting are answered: fighting during it is serious, yet abandoning Allah’s path, denying Him, desecrating the Sacred Mosque, or expelling its people are far graver sins.

islam_2_219.meaning: On intoxicants and gambling, the Qur’an notes both sin and occasional benefit, but declares the sin outweighs any gain; believers are told to avoid excess and heed divine clarification.
islam_2_219.text: On intoxicants and gambling, the Qur’an notes both sin and occasional benefit, but declares the sin outweighs any gain; believers are told to avoid excess and heed divine clarification.

islam_2_220.meaning: Discusses worldly and afterlife matters, urging kindness toward orphans; treating them as brothers protects them from exploitation, while Allah discerns corruptors from reformers, emphasizing divine justice.
islam_2_220.text: Discusses worldly and afterlife matters, urging kindness toward orphans; treating them as brothers protects them from exploitation, while Allah discerns corruptors from reformers, emphasizing divine justice.

islam_2_221.meaning: Prohibits marrying polytheist women or men until they embrace Islam; a believing slave is preferable, even if less attractive, highlighting faith’s priority over social or physical appeal.
islam_2_221.text: Prohibits marrying polytheist women or men until they embrace Islam; a believing slave is preferable, even if less attractive, highlighting faith’s priority over social or physical appeal.

islam_2_216.meaning: Combat is commanded even if disliked; what seems unpleasant may benefit, while beloved things can harm, and only He knows the true outcome.
islam_2_216.text: Combat is commanded even if disliked; what seems unpleasant may benefit, while beloved things can harm, and only He knows the true outcome.

islam_2_218.meaning: Those who believe, migrate, and fight for Allah anticipate His mercy; the passage underscores Allah’s boundless forgiveness and compassion toward sincere believers in this world and the Hereafter.
islam_2_218.text: Those who believe, migrate, and fight for Allah anticipate His mercy; the passage underscores Allah’s boundless forgiveness and compassion toward sincere believers in this world and the Hereafter.

islam_2_222.meaning: Addresses menstruation, describing it as impurity; men should refrain from sexual relations during this period until women perform ritual purification, after which normal marital intimacy may resume as ordained.
islam_2_222.text: Addresses menstruation, describing it as impurity; men should refrain from sexual relations during this period until women perform ritual purification, after which normal marital intimacy may resume as ordained.

islam_2_223.meaning: Describes wives as a field for sowing seeds, urging husbands to approach intimacy responsibly, with mindfulness of Allah, and to give glad tidings to believers about the hereafter.
islam_2_223.text: Describes wives as a field for sowing seeds, urging husbands to approach intimacy responsibly, with mindfulness of Allah, and to give glad tidings to believers about the hereafter.

islam_2_224.meaning: The verse warns against using oaths as a pretext to avoid righteousness, God-consciousness, or fairness toward others, it reminds believers that Allah fully hears and knows all intentions.
islam_2_224.text: The verse warns against using oaths as a pretext to avoid righteousness, God-consciousness, or fairness toward others, it reminds believers that Allah fully hears and knows all intentions.

islam_2_226.meaning: If a husband swears to abstain from marital relations, a waiting period of four months is prescribed; should he later reconcile, Allah’s mercy and forgiveness are affirmed.
islam_2_226.text: If a husband swears to abstain from marital relations, a waiting period of four months is prescribed; should he later reconcile, Allah’s mercy and forgiveness are affirmed.

islam_2_227.meaning: When spouses decide on divorce, the verse underscores that Allah remains fully aware of their situation, hearing all grievances and knowing the truth behind each decision.
islam_2_227.text: When spouses decide on divorce, the verse underscores that Allah remains fully aware of their situation, hearing all grievances and knowing the truth behind each decision.

islam_2_225.meaning: Unintentional breaches of oaths are not blamed, but deliberate intent is; the passage emphasizes that Allah judges the heart’s purpose and is both forgiving and patient with those who err.
islam_2_225.text: Unintentional breaches of oaths are not blamed, but deliberate intent is; the passage emphasizes that Allah judges the heart’s purpose and is both forgiving and patient with those who err.

islam_2_230.meaning: Once a divorce is final, the woman becomes unlawful for her former husband until she marries another man; if that marriage ends, both may remarry without sin.
islam_2_230.text: Once a divorce is final, the woman becomes unlawful for her former husband until she marries another man; if that marriage ends, both may remarry without sin.

islam_2_231.meaning: When a woman’s waiting period ends, the husband may keep her on just terms or release her kindly; retaining her to cause harm is prohibited and incurs sin.
islam_2_231.text: When a woman’s waiting period ends, the husband may keep her on just terms or release her kindly; retaining her to cause harm is prohibited and incurs sin.

islam_2_232.meaning: After the waiting period, if both former spouses agree on fair conditions, they may remarry; this guidance is directed to believers who uphold belief in God and the Day of Judgment.
islam_2_232.text: After the waiting period, if both former spouses agree on fair conditions, they may remarry; this guidance is directed to believers who uphold belief in God and the Day of Judgment.

islam_2_233.meaning: Mothers may breastfeed for two full years if they choose; fathers are obliged to provide food and clothing fairly, and no one is burdened beyond their capacity.
islam_2_233.text: Mothers may breastfeed for two full years if they choose; fathers are obliged to provide food and clothing fairly, and no one is burdened beyond their capacity.

islam_2_228.meaning: Divorced women must observe an ‘iddah’ of three menstrual cycles; they may not hide a pregnancy if they believe in God and the Hereafter, and husbands retain a stronger claim to reconciliation.
islam_2_228.text: Divorced women must observe an ‘iddah’ of three menstrual cycles; they may not hide a pregnancy if they believe in God and the Hereafter, and husbands retain a stronger claim to reconciliation.

islam_2_229.meaning: Divorce may be pronounced twice; after the second pronouncement, couples must either maintain a fair relationship or part kindly. Retaining gifts is prohibited unless both fear they cannot uphold Allah’s limits.
islam_2_229.text: Divorce may be pronounced twice; after the second pronouncement, couples must either maintain a fair relationship or part kindly. Retaining gifts is prohibited unless both fear they cannot uphold Allah’s limits.

islam_2_235.meaning: Marriage proposals may be spoken openly; secret promises are discouraged, though private thoughts are known to Allah. Transparency protects both parties and upholds ethical conduct in courtship.
islam_2_235.text: Marriage proposals may be spoken openly; secret promises are discouraged, though private thoughts are known to Allah. Transparency protects both parties and upholds ethical conduct in courtship.

islam_2_237.meaning: When a dowry was stipulated before a divorce that occurs prior to consummation, the woman is entitled to half of the agreed mahr unless both parties mutually waive the right.
islam_2_237.text: When a dowry was stipulated before a divorce that occurs prior to consummation, the woman is entitled to half of the agreed mahr unless both parties mutually waive the right.

islam_2_238.meaning: Believers are commanded to guard the five daily prayers, especially the ‘middle’ (Asr) prayer, and to stand before Allah with sincere devotion and humility in worship.
islam_2_238.text: Believers are commanded to guard the five daily prayers, especially the ‘middle’ (Asr) prayer, and to stand before Allah with sincere devotion and humility in worship.

islam_2_239.meaning: If fear of danger arises while traveling on foot or mount, prayer may be delayed; once safety returns, Muslims should resume remembrance of Allah, as He taught them new knowledge.
islam_2_239.text: If fear of danger arises while traveling on foot or mount, prayer may be delayed; once safety returns, Muslims should resume remembrance of Allah, as He taught them new knowledge.

islam_2_236.meaning: If a man divorces a woman before consummation and before fixing a dowry, he still must give her a mahr appropriate to his means, ensuring her financial security.
islam_2_236.text: If a man divorces a woman before consummation and before fixing a dowry, he still must give her a mahr appropriate to his means, ensuring her financial security.

islam_2_234.meaning: Widows observe an ‘iddah’ of four months and ten days after a husband’s death, ensuring lineage clarity and allowing respectful mourning; after this period they may remarry without restriction.
islam_2_234.text: Widows observe an ‘iddah’ of four months and ten days after a husband’s death, ensuring lineage clarity and allowing respectful mourning; after this period they may remarry without restriction.

islam_2_242.meaning: Allah presents clear signs and rational arguments throughout the Qur’an, inviting believers to contemplate, understand, and apply the divine guidance in their daily, spiritually aware lives.
islam_2_242.text: Allah presents clear signs and rational arguments throughout the Qur’an, inviting believers to contemplate, understand, and apply the divine guidance in their daily, spiritually aware lives.

islam_2_241.meaning: Divorced women are entitled to reasonable financial support (nafaqah) from their former husbands, proportionate to the husband’s ability, reflecting a moral duty upon the righteous.
islam_2_241.text: Divorced women are entitled to reasonable financial support (nafaqah) from their former husbands, proportionate to the husband’s ability, reflecting a moral duty upon the righteous.

islam_2_240.meaning: A deceased man must allocate a year’s maintenance for his widows from his estate before they may remarry; after this provision, they are free to act independently.
islam_2_240.text: A deceased man must allocate a year’s maintenance for his widows from his estate before they may remarry; after this provision, they are free to act independently.

islam_2_243.meaning: The Qur’an recounts how believers who migrated in large numbers were tested with death, then revived by Allah’s command, illustrating divine mercy and human tendency toward ingratitude.
islam_2_243.text: The Qur’an recounts how believers who migrated in large numbers were tested with death, then revived by Allah’s command, illustrating divine mercy and human tendency toward ingratitude.

islam_2_244.meaning: Encourages believers to engage in armed struggle for Allah's cause, emphasizing that Allah observes all actions and understands intentions, linking warfare to divine accountability and purpose.
islam_2_244.text: Encourages believers to engage in armed struggle for Allah's cause, emphasizing that Allah observes all actions and understands intentions, linking warfare to divine accountability and purpose.

islam_2_245.meaning: Invites believers to donate willingly for Allah, promising that He will increase the reward manifold; it also reminds that all provision is ultimately withheld or granted by Allah, and everyone returns to Him.
islam_2_245.text: Invites believers to donate willingly for Allah, promising that He will increase the reward manifold; it also reminds that all provision is ultimately withheld or granted by Allah, and everyone returns to Him.

islam_2_247.meaning: Prophet announces Allah's selection of Saul as king; the Israelites object, citing his lack of wealth and perceived inferiority, while the prophet reminds them that divine appointment depends solely on Allah's wisdom, not material status.
islam_2_247.text: Prophet announces Allah's selection of Saul as king; the Israelites object, citing his lack of wealth and perceived inferiority, while the prophet reminds them that divine appointment depends solely on Allah's wisdom, not material status.

islam_2_249.meaning: Saul informs his army that Allah will test them via a river; those who drink are deemed disloyal, while those who abstain demonstrate commitment, except one who drinks only a handful, showing restraint.
islam_2_249.text: Saul informs his army that Allah will test them via a river; those who drink are deemed disloyal, while those who abstain demonstrate commitment, except one who drinks only a handful, showing restraint.

islam_2_250.meaning: Before confronting Goliath, the Israelites invoke Allah, asking for patience, firm footing, and victory over the disbelieving enemy, expressing reliance on divine support in the impending battle.
islam_2_250.text: Before confronting Goliath, the Israelites invoke Allah, asking for patience, firm footing, and victory over the disbelieving enemy, expressing reliance on divine support in the impending battle.

islam_2_251.meaning: Allah grants the Israelites triumph over Goliath, appoints David as king and prophet, and endows him with divine wisdom; divine testing through appointed leaders safeguards humanity from widespread moral decay.
islam_2_251.text: Allah grants the Israelites triumph over Goliath, appoints David as king and prophet, and endows him with divine wisdom; divine testing through appointed leaders safeguards humanity from widespread moral decay.

islam_2_248.meaning: Prophet promises a sealed chest containing divine reassurance and relics from the families of Moses and Aaron, presented by angels as a tangible sign confirming Saul's rightful kingship, contingent on Allah's permission.
islam_2_248.text: Prophet promises a sealed chest containing divine reassurance and relics from the families of Moses and Aaron, presented by angels as a tangible sign confirming Saul's rightful kingship, contingent on Allah's permission.

islam_2_246.meaning: Recalls the Israelites after Moses demanding a monarch, promising to fight for Allah if a king were appointed; the prophet warns that their desire for leadership may mask reluctance to endure hardship in battle.
islam_2_246.text: Recalls the Israelites after Moses demanding a monarch, promising to fight for Allah if a king were appointed; the prophet warns that their desire for leadership may mask reluctance to endure hardship in battle.

islam_2_254.meaning: Believers are urged to donate from God-given provisions before the Day when trade, friendship, and intercession cease; the Qur’an labels those who reject this duty as wrongdoers, highlighting early Islamic emphasis on charity.
islam_2_254.text: Believers are urged to donate from God-given provisions before the Day when trade, friendship, and intercession cease; the Qur’an labels those who reject this duty as wrongdoers, highlighting early Islamic emphasis on charity.

islam_2_253.meaning: Notes that among the messengers some were elevated above others; Allah spoke directly to certain ones, raised their rank, and granted Jesus, son of Mary, unmistakable signs and support through the Holy Spirit.
islam_2_253.text: Notes that among the messengers some were elevated above others; Allah spoke directly to certain ones, raised their rank, and granted Jesus, son of Mary, unmistakable signs and support through the Holy Spirit.

islam_2_252.meaning: Declares that the revealed passages are genuine words of Allah, confirming the truth of the scripture and affirming Muhammad’s inclusion among the chosen messengers sent to humanity.
islam_2_252.text: Declares that the revealed passages are genuine words of Allah, confirming the truth of the scripture and affirming Muhammad’s inclusion among the chosen messengers sent to humanity.

islam_2_258.meaning: The narrative contrasts a ruler claiming divine power over life and death with Abraham’s affirmation that only Allah controls creation, illustrating monotheistic principle that ultimate authority belongs solely to God.
islam_2_258.text: The narrative contrasts a ruler claiming divine power over life and death with Abraham’s affirmation that only Allah controls creation, illustrating monotheistic principle that ultimate authority belongs solely to God.

islam_2_256.meaning: Faith must be chosen freely; the truth is distinguished from falsehood, so rejecting idols and embracing Allah secures a firm, unbreakable grip on guidance, while God remains all-hearing and all-knowing.
islam_2_256.text: Faith must be chosen freely; the truth is distinguished from falsehood, so rejecting idols and embracing Allah secures a firm, unbreakable grip on guidance, while God remains all-hearing and all-knowing.

islam_2_257.meaning: Allah supports believers, guiding them from spiritual darkness into illumination; disbelievers align with false powers (Taghut) that pull them deeper into darkness, destined for the fire.
islam_2_257.text: Allah supports believers, guiding them from spiritual darkness into illumination; disbelievers align with false powers (Taghut) that pull them deeper into darkness, destined for the fire.

islam_2_260.meaning: Abraham requests tangible proof of resurrection; God instructs him to split four birds, place parts on hills, then reunite them, demonstrating that God can restore life at will.
islam_2_260.text: Abraham requests tangible proof of resurrection; God instructs him to split four birds, place parts on hills, then reunite them, demonstrating that God can restore life at will.

islam_2_262.meaning: Those who give without seeking praise or causing harm receive their reward directly from God, free from fear or sorrow, emphasizing sincerity as the core of true generosity.
islam_2_262.text: Those who give without seeking praise or causing harm receive their reward directly from God, free from fear or sorrow, emphasizing sincerity as the core of true generosity.

islam_2_263.meaning: Gentle words and forgiveness surpass charitable acts that are followed by harm; God is self-sufficient and patient, highlighting moral superiority of compassion over coercive generosity.
islam_2_263.text: Gentle words and forgiveness surpass charitable acts that are followed by harm; God is self-sufficient and patient, highlighting moral superiority of compassion over coercive generosity.

islam_2_264.meaning: Believers are warned not to ruin charity by publicizing it or harming recipients, mirroring a showy spender who lacks belief in God and the Hereafter; his example is like a smooth stone.
islam_2_264.text: Believers are warned not to ruin charity by publicizing it or harming recipients, mirroring a showy spender who lacks belief in God and the Hereafter; his example is like a smooth stone.

islam_2_261.meaning: Charitable spending is likened to a seed that yields seven hundred grains, symbolizing exponential divine reward for those who give, reflecting God's limitless generosity and knowledge.
islam_2_261.text: Charitable spending is likened to a seed that yields seven hundred grains, symbolizing exponential divine reward for those who give, reflecting God's limitless generosity and knowledge.

islam_2_259.meaning: God tests a man by reviving a ruined city after a hundred-year death, showing that divine power can restore what seems lifeless, reinforcing belief in resurrection.
islam_2_259.text: God tests a man by reviving a ruined city after a hundred-year death, showing that divine power can restore what seems lifeless, reinforcing belief in resurrection.

islam_2_267.meaning: Believers are instructed to spend from lawful earnings and earth’s produce, avoiding defective items; they should give sincerely, not merely to acquire unseen benefit, trusting Allah’s awareness of their intentions.
islam_2_267.text: Believers are instructed to spend from lawful earnings and earth’s produce, avoiding defective items; they should give sincerely, not merely to acquire unseen benefit, trusting Allah’s awareness of their intentions.

islam_2_265.meaning: Those who give seeking Allah’s pleasure are compared to a high garden receiving heavy rain, producing double fruit; if the rain fails, they still have hope for future blessings.
islam_2_265.text: Those who give seeking Allah’s pleasure are compared to a high garden receiving heavy rain, producing double fruit; if the rain fails, they still have hope for future blessings.

islam_2_266.meaning: A vivid image asks if one would desire a lush orchard with rivers, abundant fruit, yet faces old age, weak heirs, and a firestorm that destroys it, illustrating the fleeting nature of worldly wealth.
islam_2_266.text: A vivid image asks if one would desire a lush orchard with rivers, abundant fruit, yet faces old age, weak heirs, and a firestorm that destroys it, illustrating the fleeting nature of worldly wealth.

islam_2_269.meaning: Divine wisdom is granted to whom He wills; possessing it is a great blessing, and only reflective, understanding hearts truly remember and appreciate this gift.
islam_2_269.text: Divine wisdom is granted to whom He wills; possessing it is a great blessing, and only reflective, understanding hearts truly remember and appreciate this gift.

islam_2_268.meaning: Satan threatens poverty and urges sin, while Allah promises forgiveness and generosity, the verse emphasizes God’s all-encompassing knowledge and mercy, encouraging reliance on divine compassion over devilish fear.
islam_2_268.text: Satan threatens poverty and urges sin, while Allah promises forgiveness and generosity, the verse emphasizes God’s all-encompassing knowledge and mercy, encouraging reliance on divine compassion over devilish fear.

islam_2_270.meaning: Every expenditure and vow is known to Allah; for those who commit wrongdoing, no ally will support them, underscoring divine surveillance and the futility of relying on worldly assistance.
islam_2_270.text: Every expenditure and vow is known to Allah; for those who commit wrongdoing, no ally will support them, underscoring divine surveillance and the futility of relying on worldly assistance.

islam_2_271.meaning: Public charity is commendable, yet secret giving to the needy is superior; it erases sins, and Allah remains fully aware of all actions, reinforcing sincerity over show.
islam_2_271.text: Public charity is commendable, yet secret giving to the needy is superior; it erases sins, and Allah remains fully aware of all actions, reinforcing sincerity over show.

islam_2_274.meaning: This verse commends those who generously give their wealth at any time, privately or publicly. Their reward is with their Lord in heaven, ensuring they won't fear future hardships or sorrows.
islam_2_274.text: This verse commends those who generously give their wealth at any time, privately or publicly. Their reward is with their Lord in heaven, ensuring they won't fear future hardships or sorrows.

islam_2_275.meaning: This verse prohibits taking or giving interest, as it misguides people comparing it to legitimate trade. Allah allows trade while forbidding unjust interest.
islam_2_275.text: This verse prohibits taking or giving interest, as it misguides people comparing it to legitimate trade. Allah allows trade while forbidding unjust interest.

islam_2_276.meaning: This verse from Surah Al-Baqarah highlights the Quranic prohibition of usury (interest) and encourages generosity through charitable giving. Allah promotes fair trade and supports the growth of investments, while discouraging disbelievers who persist in sinful practices.
islam_2_276.text: This verse from Surah Al-Baqarah highlights the Quranic prohibition of usury (interest) and encourages generosity through charitable giving. Allah promotes fair trade and supports the growth of investments, while discouraging disbelievers who persist in sinful practices.

islam_2_273.meaning: The verse describes impoverished believers restricted from moving freely for Allah’s cause; outsiders may mistake them for self-sufficient, but their visible signs reveal genuine need and reliance on divine aid.
islam_2_273.text: The verse describes impoverished believers restricted from moving freely for Allah’s cause; outsiders may mistake them for self-sufficient, but their visible signs reveal genuine need and reliance on divine aid.

islam_2_272.meaning: Guidance belongs solely to Allah, who directs whom He wills; any good spent is ultimately for the donor’s benefit, driven by the desire to please God, and will be fully repaid.
islam_2_272.text: Guidance belongs solely to Allah, who directs whom He wills; any good spent is ultimately for the donor’s benefit, driven by the desire to please God, and will be fully repaid.

islam_2_278.meaning: This verse from Surah Al-Baqarah encourages believers to fear Allah and refrain from usury (excessive interest). Adhering to this instruction promotes fairness and ethical business practices.
islam_2_278.text: This verse from Surah Al-Baqarah encourages believers to fear Allah and refrain from usury (excessive interest). Adhering to this instruction promotes fairness and ethical business practices.

islam_2_277.meaning: This verse from Surah Al-Baqarah (2:277) emphasizes the reward of righteous deeds. Believers who perform good deeds, pray, and give charity will have peace and joy in the Hereafter.
islam_2_277.text: This verse from Surah Al-Baqarah (2:277) emphasizes the reward of righteous deeds. Believers who perform good deeds, pray, and give charity will have peace and joy in the Hereafter.

islam_2_279.meaning: This verse (2:279) from Surah Al-Baqarah instructs Muslims to forgive debts and accept only the original amount given for loans. If they fail to do so, they risk a war declaration from Allah and His Messenger.
islam_2_279.text: This verse (2:279) from Surah Al-Baqarah instructs Muslims to forgive debts and accept only the original amount given for loans. If they fail to do so, they risk a war declaration from Allah and His Messenger.

islam_2_280.meaning: This verse (2:280) encourages postponing financial demands from those experiencing difficulties, emphasizing compassion and relief. Giving charity is also highlighted as beneficial, emphasizing generosity and spiritual growth.
islam_2_280.text: This verse (2:280) encourages postponing financial demands from those experiencing difficulties, emphasizing compassion and relief. Giving charity is also highlighted as beneficial, emphasizing generosity and spiritual growth.

islam_2_281.meaning: This verse from Surah Al-Baqarah (2:281) emphasizes the Day of Judgement, where each person will be recompensed for their deeds. It encourages Muslims to lead righteous lives and avoid injustice, ensuring accountability and mercy.
islam_2_281.text: This verse from Surah Al-Baqarah (2:281) emphasizes the Day of Judgement, where each person will be recompensed for their deeds. It encourages Muslims to lead righteous lives and avoid injustice, ensuring accountability and mercy.

islam_2_282.meaning: This verse (2:282) emphasizes the importance of written agreements in Islam. It commands believers to record debts with clear terms, ensuring fairness for all parties involved.
islam_2_282.text: This verse (2:282) emphasizes the importance of written agreements in Islam. It commands believers to record debts with clear terms, ensuring fairness for all parties involved.

islam_2_284.meaning: This verse (2:284) highlights that everything in the heavens and on earth belongs to Allah. Whether you conceal or reveal your thoughts, He knows them all. He forgives and punishes as He wills.
islam_2_284.text: This verse (2:284) highlights that everything in the heavens and on earth belongs to Allah. Whether you conceal or reveal your thoughts, He knows them all. He forgives and punishes as He wills.

islam_2_285.meaning: This verse (2:285) is from the Quranic surah Al-Baqarah. It highlights the faith of the Prophet Muhammad (صلى الله عليه وسلم) and the believers in Allah, His angels, Books (holy texts), and messengers without تمييز. It encourages unity and respect among all divine messengers.
islam_2_285.text: This verse (2:285) is from the Quranic surah Al-Baqarah. It highlights the faith of the Prophet Muhammad (صلى الله عليه وسلم) and the believers in Allah, His angels, Books (holy texts), and messengers without تمييز. It encourages unity and respect among all divine messengers.

islam_2_283.meaning: This verse discusses the guidelines for temporary situations when formal writing and witnesses are unavailable. It prescribes taking a security deposit (gharar) or a written promise as a substitute when unable to find a scribe. Honoring trusts, fearing Allah, and not hiding knowledge are emphasized.
islam_2_283.text: This verse discusses the guidelines for temporary situations when formal writing and witnesses are unavailable. It prescribes taking a security deposit (gharar) or a written promise as a substitute when unable to find a scribe. Honoring trusts, fearing Allah, and not hiding knowledge are emphasized.

islam_al_baqarah_2_1.meaning: The disjointed letters Alif-Lam-Meem open many Meccan surahs; their precise meaning remains unknown, yet scholars view them as a divine challenge, a reminder of Qur’anic inimitability.
islam_al_baqarah_2_1.text: The disjointed letters Alif-Lam-Meem open many Meccan surahs; their precise meaning remains unknown, yet scholars view them as a divine challenge, a reminder of Qur’anic inimitability.

islam_al_baqarah_2_2.meaning: Declares the Qur’an as a book free of doubt, a clear guide for mutawattiʿūn (those conscious of Allah), emphasizing its role as moral and legal compass.
islam_al_baqarah_2_2.text: Declares the Qur’an as a book free of doubt, a clear guide for mutawattiʿūn (those conscious of Allah), emphasizing its role as moral and legal compass.

islam_al_baqarah_2_3.meaning: Specifies the believers’ characteristics: belief in the unseen (ghayb), establishing regular prayer (ṣalāh), and giving charity from God-provided sustenance, illustrating faith expressed through worship and social responsibility.
islam_al_baqarah_2_3.text: Specifies the believers’ characteristics: belief in the unseen (ghayb), establishing regular prayer (ṣalāh), and giving charity from God-provided sustenance, illustrating faith expressed through worship and social responsibility.

islam_al_baqarah_2_4.meaning: Belief includes acceptance of the Qur'an revealed to Muhammad, earlier scriptures given to previous prophets, and certainty about the Hereafter. It describes the core creed of Islam linking past revelations with future accountability.
islam_al_baqarah_2_4.text: Belief includes acceptance of the Qur'an revealed to Muhammad, earlier scriptures given to previous prophets, and certainty about the Hereafter. It describes the core creed of Islam linking past revelations with future accountability.

islam_al_baqarah_2_5.meaning: Those guided by Allah’s direction are described as successful; success is defined as attaining divine guidance, which leads to moral uprightness, spiritual fulfillment, and ultimate reward in the afterlife.
islam_al_baqarah_2_5.text: Those guided by Allah’s direction are described as successful; success is defined as attaining divine guidance, which leads to moral uprightness, spiritual fulfillment, and ultimate reward in the afterlife.

islam_al_baqarah_2_163.meaning: The declaration affirms monotheism: Allah alone is God, without partners, described as the All-Merciful and Especially Merciful, forming the core creed of Islamic belief for humanity.
islam_al_baqarah_2_163.text: The declaration affirms monotheism: Allah alone is God, without partners, described as the All-Merciful and Especially Merciful, forming the core creed of Islamic belief for humanity.

islam_al_baqarah_2_255.meaning: Allah is declared sole deity, eternal and self-sustaining; He never sleeps nor tires. All creation belongs to Him, and no one can intercede except by His permission, underscoring divine sovereignty.
islam_al_baqarah_2_255.text: Allah is declared sole deity, eternal and self-sustaining; He never sleeps nor tires. All creation belongs to Him, and no one can intercede except by His permission, underscoring divine sovereignty.

islam_al_baqarah_2_286.meaning: This verse (2:286) from Surah Al-Baqarah highlights Allah's teachings on individual responsibility and mercy. It declares that Allah does not hold people accountable for the actions of others or their predestination. Instead, they are judged based on their own choices and efforts.
islam_al_baqarah_2_286.text: This verse (2:286) from Surah Al-Baqarah highlights Allah's teachings on individual responsibility and mercy. It declares that Allah does not hold people accountable for the actions of others or their predestination. Instead, they are judged based on their own choices and efforts.
